name: Incident workstreams

groups.label: Evaluation
groups.definition: Training precursors, evaluation experiments, and changes to tools or transcripts used in evaluation.

groups.label: Access
groups.definition: Artifactory access, external footholds and staging, credential discovery, and cloud reconnaissance.

groups.label: Coordination
groups.definition: Evaluation coordination, agent communication, decisions, restraint, and recruitment.

groups.label: Intrusion
groups.definition: Activity grouped in the source phases around organizational intrusion, protected data or build systems, data transport, supply-chain poisoning, and concealment. Membership does not establish that an attempted effect succeeded.
phases: Sol participation in Hugging Face intrusion

groups.label: Response
groups.definition: Containment, remediation, agent termination, and loss of access as grouped by the original phase labels. Membership does not establish protective intent or effectiveness.

groups.label: Investigation
groups.definition: Investigation, disclosure, and remediation recorded in the source phases centered on investigation or vendor follow-up.

assignment_policy: Each of the 27 existing phase labels is assigned to exactly one display workstream, covering all 832 records without changing the canonical data or adding inferred event facts. These six workstreams are navigation groups, not a causal sequence, risk ontology, severity judgment, or evidence judgment. Mixed source phases are kept intact: Internal database access and investigation belongs to Intrusion; Evaluation and coordination belongs to Coordination; Investigation and remediation and Vendor remediation and disclosure belong to Investigation. Consequently a workstream can include activities that also fit another group. The original phase remains available on each event.

display_conventions.fill: Six distinct jewel hues identify workstream: gold, turquoise, lilac, orange, jade and blue. Perceptual lightness and chroma are balanced across the palette while preserving clear warm and cool differences. Color has no severity, outcome or evidential meaning. Foreground fills retain their categorical color over a dark neutral separating keyline; transition opacity and selection are display emphasis only.
display_conventions.outline: Foreground edges retain the workstream color and evidence geometry. A dark neutral keyline (#0B1117) separates overlapping colors at their existing coordinates, and a background-colored interior masks marks behind hollow or broken shapes. Context uses a hollow shape; Unresolved uses a broken outline. No additional spacing or causal grouping is inferred from this treatment. Hover, selection and keyboard focus may add restrained emphasis without changing the workstream or evidence category.
display_conventions.severity: The Impact field is an umbrella for adverse effects, Near-misses and Preventive actions. It contains numerical 0–5 severity and the separate unnumbered − Preventive category. Context and Unresolved have their own flat fields, selected with assessment controls; they never occupy lower positions on the ordered impact scale. Neutral boxed numbers and attached criteria communicate severity. Neither color nor drawn marker size encodes severity.
display_conventions.shape: Shape independently identifies evidence status: circle for Reported, diamond for Reasoning, triangle for Inferred, and a six-point polygonal star for Accounts differ. Areas are approximately equal within each single/grouped size class.
display_conventions.hollow: Hollow foreground shapes identify the completed Context assessment disposition. They do not mean uncertain dates, missing source evidence or a Near-miss. The shape geometry still identifies Reported, Reasoning, Inferred or Accounts differ, and the visible edge retains the workstream color.
display_conventions.time_uncertainty: Finite date-window marks and attached temporal evidence communicate date uncertainty. The 12 records without a supported earliest date retain their own IDs in the selected impact or separate assessment field, with selectable curved trails that fade to the left. Each head marks the inferred exclusive upper boundary at 2026-07-14T00:00:00Z, labeled By 13 July, rather than an observed event time. The fading left end means the start is unknown; it invents neither a start date nor a duration. A head outside the visible time range remains outside instead of being clamped to the edge; its visible trail remains selectable. Curvature distinguishes the trail from an observed chronology and does not encode a changing impact, path, or causal sequence.
display_conventions.legend: Six labeled workstream swatches retain the same rich base palette in each view. Legend labels, filtering and attached workstream names also identify each group. Evidence shapes, assessment fills and a neutral size key explain the independent encodings; color alone is never the only group label.
display_conventions.size: Two visibly distinct sizes identify source scope: radius 2.3 CSS pixels for a single event and 4.4 for grouped activity at the base desktop scale. Grouped means the source combines actions without describing each individually. This is a binary category, not a proportional count, severity, confidence or importance. Equal-area evidence geometry and temporary zoom/selection magnification remain. Existing positions are retained.

recommended_opacity.meaning: Display emphasis only. Opacity is not confidence, severity, probability, recency or event multiplicity.

display_conventions.unresolved: A broken foreground outline identifies the completed Unresolved assessment disposition. It preserves the original evidence-status shape and workstream color; the specific missing or conflicting assessment evidence remains attached to the record.
display_conventions.background_density: A neutral field illustrates the larger source-reported activity that is not individually resolved in this dataset. Responsive rendering uses 5,000–22,000 tiny density marks. This is a rendering density, not an event count or an expansion of the 832 records. Marks have no event IDs, individual timestamps, severity values or evidence classifications; their positions are illustrative. A hidden egg in the title-page footer unlocks number-only decorative catalogue labels on hover or tap. Before unlocking, background points expose no labels. The background contributes nothing to record or filter counts.
display_conventions.open_left_trails: No separate undated row or DOM comet buttons are used. The 12 open-left records retain their canonical IDs in the selected impact or separate assessment field. Canvas hit-testing can select their heads or curved visible trails, and keyboard users can open them through the register. The head is an inferred upper-bound marker, not the date of occurrence. Trail length and curvature do not encode duration, impact change or a causal trajectory.
display_conventions.assessment_views: Impact contains 599 entries, Context 192 and Unresolved 41. Impact includes adverse effects, Near-misses and Preventive actions. These unnumbered controls switch between an ordered impact field and two separate fields without numerical ranking. Context and Unresolved retain their completed review dispositions and source evidence; neither is zero, negative severity, or a continuation below Preventive.
display_conventions.view_navigation: The primary view labels are View #1: Event-swarm and View #2: Bow-tie; the optional systems inquiry is Bonus: Investigate!. View numbers distinguish layouts, not assessment values.
display_conventions.lifecycle_navigation: Full, I. Before, II. During and III. After group existing incident roles. Roman numerals identify lifecycle sections, not exact non-overlapping date windows. Impact, Context and Unresolved remain unnumbered alternatives, not additional lifecycle steps or a severity ranking.
display_conventions.light: The six existing workstream colors are unchanged. Cached high-resolution marker sprites add low-opacity colored halos and a restrained surface highlight. A narrow dark edge separates overlapping silhouettes. The background retains thousands of neutral illustrative density marks, with a faint decorative ribbon using the same six hues. Light and atmospheric color encode no additional variable.
display_conventions.incident_overview: A single iridescent form represents the incident as a collection of connected attacks, decisions, responses and findings. At the top-level page opening it dissolves into 832 illustrative particles and reveals the introduction. Entering the event field resolves the compact form into the currently plotted events. The opening is decorative, not an additional event, a severity assessment, chronology or claim that every event is causally connected. Reduced motion and deep links skip the entrance animation. Pointer, keyboard, scroll, resize or backgrounding dismiss the short opening immediately.

migration_note: Version 6.1 restores luminous rendering of the existing six workstream colors, makes single/grouped sizes visibly distinct, and adds a one-to-many opening form. All event assignments, dates, severity assessments and canonical fields remain unchanged.

palette_calibration.gamut_policy: Orange and blue chroma are reduced to remain in the sRGB gamut at their selected hue and lightness. Values are rounded to 8-bit sRGB for rendering.
palette_calibration.purpose: Provide clearly distinct warm and cool jewel colors with substantial chroma and similar readable lightness against the dark field. No claim of a universal optimal palette or color-vision equivalence is made; labels, filters and source-record names remain available.

source_counts.relationship: Clusters group these same actions; they are not an additional action total.

The roughly 1.2 million message-board entries mainly encode fragments of these files and messages within a larger roughly 20 million-entry cache dump. Those raw-entry counts are not additional attacks.

background_activity.overlap_policy: The HF action count and METR communication count have different scopes and can overlap. Do not add them, treat them as independent totals, or subtract 832 to calculate an unseen remainder. Displayable entries, source aggregates and raw log/cache records have different units.
background_activity.caption: Faint stars suggest the larger source-reported activity behind the detailed record. Approximately 17,600 recovered HF actions and over 70,000 messages and files were reported. Counts overlap; stars are illustrative, not individually identified events.
background_activity.selection_meaning: The egg beside the main field Legend unlocks a decorative star number and local magnifying shimmer. No historical event identity or incident details are assigned.
background_activity.catalogue_numbering: Stable indices 1–70000, padded to five digits. Every index is drawn once at every viewport size. Each has a distinct placement cell, with a soft edge and density calibration.
background_activity.unlock_control: Small egg beside the peripheral Legend on the event screen
